title: [YouPass Collect] - Reasons for immigrants to and from a European country in 2009
prompt: The charts below show the reasons for immigrants to and from a European country in 2009. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts compare the proportions of various reasons why people immigrated to and emigrated from a European nation in 2009.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, having a definite job was the primary motivation for those leaving the country, while family-related reasons were most common among those arriving. Additionally, work and study collectively accounted for a larger share of emigration than immigration.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding professional and educational motivations, 38% of emigrants left with a confirmed job offer, which was significantly higher than 23% of immigrants arriving for the same reason. In terms of job-seeking, those moving to the country accounted for 15%, marginally exceeding 13% of those departing. Meanwhile, study represented 15% of arrivals, more than double the 7% recorded for departures.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for personal factors, accompanying family members was cited by a quarter of immigrants, substantially more than 15% of emigrants leaving for this purpose. By con, only 15% of people moving to this country said that they did so for other unspecified reasons, slightly lower compared to 17% of emigrants. Finally, the percentage of people with no stated reason remained relatively minor in both groups, at 7% for immigrants and 4% for emigrants.
